text: I'm the game master. Last night we played the first session of the Brackwater adventure, and its transcript is already stored. Please debrief it with me. Write in English.

Follow nextCursor as cursor with the same arguments while truncated, even on an empty page. Do the same when reading scene transcripts or entity history. total is only complete when totalIsExact is true. If this is first use, adventure_start creates the campaign and starter schema; session_create records the played date in the current adventure. The first debrief seeds from the latest session and, if offered, the earlier session note. Do not bulk-import older sessions.
Load skill map-speakers and skill split-scenes. If the session has no stored transcript, call transcript_upload_url. With a shell and a file on disk, run curl -T <file> <signed-url> directly from disk. Never read, echo, cat or repeat the file to upload it. The signed URL is single-use and expires after ten minutes.
Without a shell or without the original file on disk, immediately give the game master pageUrl to sign in and upload the original transcript file. Pause until they have uploaded it. Do not retype the transcript in tool calls or chat, even when you hold it in context.
Both paths use UTF-8 [HH:MM:SS] Speaker: text with continuation lines, at most 8 MB and 20000 utterances, 32 KB per utterance including continuations. Upload before scenes or draft changes exist. Read get transcript:<session> to confirm it is stored before mapping speakers, splitting scenes or starting the debrief. If the transcript is still missing, wait for the upload.
Use the stored utterances and scenes.
Walk each scene in order. Use find by name and aliases before creating an entity. Record every named NPC who speaks or is named in play, but keep a person existing only in a rumor inside that rumor. For each NPC the game master voiced, fill playedAs from the actual voice and manner. Preserve spelling variants as aliases. Do not invent motives, secrets, properties or kinds. Fill only fields supported by the session. Leave out mechanics, rolls, rests, hit points and inventory.
Each change needs scene, change, a non-empty basis list, at least one short verbatim source {quote, at?}, and why. Use basis narrated for narration, npc_said for an NPC claim, rumor for a rumor, player_guess or player_plan for those, and game_master for the GM's own answer. With npc_said identify the speaking NPC in the quote or why. A basis consisting only of player_guess/player_plan may touch only thread or character_goal, never an NPC, place, world fact or clock. Facts, claims, rumors and guesses must stay apart.
Operations are new {kind,name,tempKey?,aliases?,properties?}, update {entity,properties?,addAliases?}, relate/unrelate {type,from,to}. Entity refs are ids or $tempKey from an earlier accepted new change in this draft. Read the allowed properties, enum values and relationship endpoint kinds from schema. A relationship touches both endpoints. Merge repeated updates within a scene where possible.
Catch what the briefing needs. A tie between NPCs in play the table showed (partners, rivals, a boss, kin) goes into both NPCs' relationships, naming the other NPC and the tie, with the quote that shows it. A deadline the table named becomes a clock: new clock with countsToward the deadline in the table's words, segments and filled from what was said, and visibleToPlayers, then relate pressures from the clock to its thread. A condition an NPC set on a thread goes into the thread's whatIsOpen with basis npc_said, naming the NPC and the condition. Never invent a tie, a deadline or a condition the table did not show.
Call debrief_add with the proposed changes. It keeps valid changes and rejects invalid ones individually with allowed lists. Fix a rejected change; do not work around its rule. Read get debrief:<session> in scene order. Clients with MCP Apps show the Ledger view for debrief_add and debrief_drop, where the game master can drop changes; read get debrief:<session> again before debrief_commit. To fix a kept change, debrief_drop its id and add the replacement. Dropping a parent refuses to break dependent changes and names them by scene and subject, as the Ledger shows them; find their ids in get debrief:<session>. Drop them together, then add replacements in dependency order.
The review is the draft briefing. Load skill briefing and write the briefing it describes from the committed story state plus this draft, as if the draft were committed, with its parts, word budgets, sources, claim marks and flags. This debrief is its transcript pass: put what the story state lacks into the draft as changes, never into store corrections, and leave that part out. Store it with debrief_add as briefing, within 16 KB, and store it again whenever it changes.
Open the review with the draft briefing, with at most one line before it. Then ask at most five review questions, numbered, each one single question in one sentence with a transcript timestamp, aimed at one gap the briefing had to work around: a deadline the table named without a clock, a tie between NPCs in play, a condition an NPC set on a thread, an NPC whose role the transcript leaves unclear, or a player character who stayed silent. Never put two questions in one item. Ask only what changes story state and never what the players will decide. Deliberate GM vagueness stays as said and is not a question. Questions stay in chat, not the store. End with numbered options: answer the questions (recommended while any are open), commit the debrief as it stands, or see the per-change detail. Never list drafted or rejected changes or schema limits in the review; show changes by scene only when the game master asks for that detail.
Each answer becomes a draft change with debrief_add, basis game_master and their words as source, in the scene its question's timestamp falls in. Then rewrite the affected lines of the briefing, store it with debrief_add and show the review again in the same shape: at most one line saying the answers are in the draft, the revised briefing, the questions still open, and the options. Never report the answer changes one by one.
Call debrief_commit only after the game master says the draft is right. It applies the entire draft, appends history and keeps the briefing in the store atomically; a commit without a briefing is refused. The stored briefing opens the next prep. A committed debrief never changes; later fixes use story_commit with a reason and the game master's answer as source.

Standing rules
Give before you ask. The creative part belongs to the game master; they decide.
Pitch only where the procedure calls for it: small, droppable situations built on named story-state facts with sources, never outcomes and never what the players choose. The section's definition sets their shape and count. A pitch adds pressure to the players' plan and must never block it or a scene the game master prepared.
Only the game master's picks enter the note. An ignored pitch leaves no trace.
Ask about situations and pressure, never player decisions or outcomes.
Story state records what happened. The adventure frame records intent. Keep them apart.
Write in the game master's language.","skills":[]}

scenes.summary: The party arrives with the supply cart and asks about a red-cloaked courier. Hedda Brask keeps the toll ledger shut; her husband Osric, the ferryman, says the causeway was dry three days ago.

scenes.title: The warden's deadline
scenes.summary: Warden Calloway says the spring tide drowns the causeway in four days and her pay chest crossed with the courier. Hedda will open the ledger only for Osric's ferry bell from the drowned chapel.

scenes.title: The drowned chapel

scenes.title: Fire at the tollhouse
scenes.summary: Back at the tollhouse, Osric says the morning low tide comes at the fifth bell and gives an hour in the chapel.

{"name":"briefing","procedure":"Open prep with this one-page briefing before the game master says anything. It answers where the party stands and what pulls; it gives before it asks. Use the language the game master explicitly requests; otherwise the language of their current message. Prep never starts an adventure or changes the current one; if none exists, ask the game master to start one.
Read first. get overview for the stored briefing, the current adventure and its frame.
At prep, when get overview returns a briefing, open with its text exactly as stored, without regenerating it, rereading the store for it or making a transcript pass. When its correctionsSince is not empty, insert one short part "Since the debrief" before its What next part, one line per correction with its reason. Then go on as its What next part says. Compose a new briefing as below when get overview returns none, and always when the debrief loads this procedure for its review. find without a query for every entity; follow nextCursor with the same arguments until totalIsExact, and never brief from a partial page. get entity:<id> for the threads, NPCs, clocks, character goals and places, keeping each change's basis, source quote and timestamp. When get offers the game master's secrets, read the open ones. Then make at most one pass over the latest session's transcript with find and get transcript:<session> for what the story state lacks: a deadline the table named without a clock, a tie between NPCs in play, a condition an NPC set on a thread, a thread the players cared about. One pass, never a second debrief.
Write 400 to 600 words, counting sources, headings and the what-next options. Keep to each part's word budget below, sources included; together they make about 500 words. Start with the first part, without a preamble. Plot first, no mechanics, no tables: plain chat text with short headings and short lines, in exactly this order. When a part runs long, shorten its lines; never drop a part.
1. Where the party stands (about 40 words): two or three lines with place, time, the last thing that happened and the plan the players announced.
2. What pulls (about 100 words): three to five threads, strongest pull first, one or two lines each with where it stands and what pulls the party toward it now. A thread that serves the frame's goal ranks higher.
3. Forgotten threads (about 40 words): one to three threads the players cared about that nothing moved, one line each with why it might matter now.
4. NPCs in play (about 100 words): the three to six NPCs the next session is likely to meet, one line each with how they were played, what they want and their tie to another NPC in play. Write "not played yet" for an empty playedAs and "wants unknown" for an empty wants; never invent a want or a tie.
5. Clocks and pressure (about 50 words): every clock with its value, measured against the frame's timeframe, then the pressure that has no clock.
6. Off-screen moves (about 100 words): two or three pitches to pick from. Each names who acts, what they do while the party is busy, the situation that lands on the table, and "Built on:" with its named facts and sources.
7. Store corrections (about 30 words): only when the transcript pass found something the story state lacks, one line each with its source. Leave this part out otherwise.
8. Frame flags (about 15 words): one line saying the frame is empty, or one line for each frame field the last session put in question. Leave this part out when the frame needs nothing.
9. What next (about 30 words): two or three numbered options, the recommended one first, and no other question. When the frame is empty, the recommended option is a short frame talk. When only fields are flagged, offer that frame talk second. Other options include confirming the store corrections, then the first checklist section, or picking an off-screen move and going to the first section.
Source every fact: [HH:MM:SS] for the latest session, [S<n> HH:MM:SS] for an older session, or the entity name when the fact has no quote. Mark claims by who made them: according to <NPC>, rumor, player guess, player plan. A line an NPC speaks is that NPC's claim, also when it is about another NPC or a tie between them. Narration and the game master's answers stand bare. Mark a secret "(secret)" and never write it as something the players know. A gap is a flag, never filled with an invented fact, motive or clock. Prefer short quotes of the game master's and NPCs' own words for flavor.
Store corrections wait for the game master's okay. Only then write them with story_commit, a reason, the basis they had at the table and their transcript lines as sources, and confirm with get entity:<id>. The briefing writes nothing else. When the game master picks an option, load its procedure: frame-talk for the frame talk, prep-sparring for the checklist.

properties.nextStep: Go to the drowned chapel at low water tomorrow morning (player plan).

sources.quote: Out on the marsh path, the chapel's bell tower leans over the reeds.
At the chapel door the water is ankle deep and rising. Inside, something knocks against the pews in the current.
Ilka: We mark the door and come back at low water, like we said.

changes.why: What the party saw at the chapel.

Where the party stands
Night at the Brackwater tollhouse, by Osric's fire [00:19:30]. Ilka, Rook and Brother Fen found the drowned chapel flooding, marked its door and turned back [00:18:45]. Player plan: return at low water tomorrow morning [00:14:05].

What pulls
- Osric's ferry bell: Hedda's price for the ledger. According to Hedda: "You bring that bell back to me and I open the ledger for you. Not before." [00:12:50]. According to Osric, low tide at the fifth bell gives "an hour in that chapel, no more" [00:20:10].
- Find the red-cloaked courier: the party's aim [00:02:20]. Who crossed with them is in Hedda's ledger, which "stays shut for strangers" [00:04:10].
- Calloway's pay chest: according to Calloway it crossed with the courier; it must be back at the garrison before the tide, or "I hang somebody for it" [00:10:05].
- The grey-cloaked woman: watched from the tollhouse roof, then gone [00:15:30]. Only Rook saw her [00:16:40].

Forgotten threads
- Nothing yet; every thread is one session old. The grey woman is the closest: Rook asked about her and nobody followed up [00:16:10].

NPCs in play
- Hedda Brask, toll keeper: broad, slow-spoken, never looks up from the ledger [00:01:40]. Wants the ferry bell back [00:12:50]. Married to Osric for twenty years, according to Osric [00:05:50].
- Osric Brask, ferryman: lean, talks fast, laughs at his own jokes [00:06:20]. Wants unknown. According to Osric, the bell was his father's [00:13:20]. "Hedda takes the toll, I take the oars. Brask and Brask." [00:06:45]
- Warden Calloway: curt, mud to the knees, never dismounts, rides off without waiting for an answer [00:09:10, 00:10:40]. Wants her pay chest back before the tide [00:10:05]. No tie to the Brasks shown.

Clocks and pressure
- Spring tide: 0/4, shown to players. According to Calloway, four days, then "the causeway is gone until midsummer" [00:09:40]. There is no frame timeframe to measure it against.
- Without a clock: the chapel floods at high water, according to Osric [00:13:20]. The causeway is already half under water [00:00:15].

Off-screen moves
1. Calloway sends someone to keep watch. At dawn a garrison trooper waits at the tollhouse, wants to know what the party has learned for the warden, and watches who crosses. Built on: Calloway's pay chest [00:10:05]; she rode toward the garrison [00:10:40].
2. Someone got to the chapel first. At the fifth bell the party finds fresh, wet footprints leading through their marked door. Built on: the grey-cloaked woman on the roof [00:15:30]; the marked door [00:18:45]; low tide at the fifth bell [00:20:10].
3. The drowning causeway calls Osric away. At dawn a stranded carter shouts for the ferry, and Osric must row just as the party sets out. Built on: the causeway half under water [00:00:15]; "When the causeway drowns, I row folk across" [00:06:45].

Frame flags
- The frame is empty: no goal, timeframe, stakes or finale yet.

What next
1. A short frame talk for Brackwater: goal, timeframe and stakes (recommended).
2. Pick an off-screen move, then go to the first prep section.
3. Go straight to the first prep section.

I split session 1 into four scenes and drafted the changes. This is the draft briefing:

**Where the party stands**
Night at the Brackwater tollhouse, by Osric's fire [00:19:30]. Ilka, Rook and Brother Fen found the drowned chapel flooding, marked its door and turned back [00:18:45]. Player plan: return at low water tomorrow morning [00:14:05].

**What pulls**
- **Osric's ferry bell:** this is Hedda's price for the ledger. According to Hedda: "You bring that bell back to me and I open the ledger for you. Not before." [00:12:50]. According to Osric, low tide at the fifth bell gives "an hour in that chapel, no more" [00:20:10].
- **Find the red-cloaked courier:** the party's aim [00:02:20]. Who crossed with them is in Hedda's ledger, which "stays shut for strangers" [00:04:10].
- **Calloway's pay chest:** according to Calloway it crossed with the courier. It must be back at the garrison before the tide, or "I hang somebody for it" [00:10:05].
- **The grey-cloaked woman:** she watched from the tollhouse roof, then was gone [00:15:30]. Only Rook saw her [00:16:40].

**Forgotten threads**
- Nothing yet, because every thread is one session old. The grey woman comes closest: Rook asked about her and nobody followed up [00:16:10].

**NPCs in play**
- **Hedda Brask, toll keeper:** broad and slow-spoken, never looks up from the ledger [00:01:40]. Wants the ferry bell back [00:12:50]. Married to Osric for twenty years, according to Osric [00:05:50].
- **Osric Brask, ferryman:** lean, talks fast, laughs at his own jokes [00:06:20]. Wants unknown. According to Osric, the bell was his father's [00:13:20]. "Hedda takes the toll, I take the oars. Brask and Brask." [00:06:45]
- **Warden Calloway:** curt, mud to the knees, never dismounts, rides off without waiting for an answer [00:09:10, 00:10:40]. Wants her pay chest back before the tide [00:10:05]. No tie to the Brasks shown.

**Clocks and pressure**
- **Spring tide:** 0/4, shown to players. According to Calloway it comes in four days, and then "the causeway is gone until midsummer" [00:09:40]. There is no frame timeframe to measure it against.
- **No clock:**
  - According to Osric, the chapel floods at high water [00:13:20].
  - The causeway is already half under water [00:00:15].

**Off-screen moves**
1. **Calloway sends someone to keep watch.** At dawn a garrison trooper waits at the tollhouse, wants to know what the party has learned for the warden, and watches who crosses. *Built on:* Calloway's pay chest [00:10:05]; she rode toward the garrison [00:10:40].
2. **Someone got to the chapel first.** At the fifth bell the party finds fresh, wet footprints leading through their marked door. *Built on:* the grey-cloaked woman on the roof [00:15:30]; the marked door [00:18:45]; low tide at the fifth bell [00:20:10].
3. **The drowning causeway calls Osric away.** At dawn a stranded carter shouts for the ferry, and Osric has to row just as the party sets out. *Built on:* the causeway half under water [00:00:15]; "When the causeway drowns, I row folk across" [00:06:45].

**Frame flags**
- The frame is empty: no goal, timeframe, stakes or finale yet.

**What next**
1. A short frame talk for Brackwater: goal, timeframe and stakes (recommended).
2. Pick an off-screen move, then go to the first prep section.
3. Go straight to the first prep section.

---

**Review questions**
1. [00:00:15] Brother Fen never speaks in the transcript, so what is Brother Fen's concept?
2. [00:02:20] What are Ilka's and Rook's concepts?
3. [00:09:10] Is Warden Calloway tied to Hedda or Osric Brask in any way?
4. [00:09:40] Did Calloway's four days start at that dusk, so that the Spring tide clock stays at 0 of 4?
5. [00:10:05] Who is the courier: someone with a name and a role who should be recorded as an NPC, or only an unnamed figure in the threads for now?

**How to continue**
1. Answer the questions (recommended while any are open).
2. Commit the debrief as it stands.
3. See the per-change detail by scene.

input.briefing:
Where the party stands
Night at the Brackwater tollhouse, by Osric's fire [00:19:30]. The party found the drowned chapel flooding, marked its door and turned back [00:18:45]. Brother Fen guarded the cart throughout and heard everything, but said nothing (game master). Player plan: return at low water tomorrow morning [00:14:05].

What pulls
- Osric's ferry bell: Hedda's condition stands, the bell first, then the ledger (game master). According to Hedda: "You bring that bell back to me and I open the ledger for you. Not before." [00:12:50]. According to Osric, low tide at the fifth bell gives "an hour in that chapel, no more" [00:20:10].
- Find the red-cloaked courier: the party's aim [00:02:20]. Who crossed with them is in Hedda's ledger, which "stays shut for strangers" [00:04:10].
- Calloway's pay chest: according to Calloway it crossed with the courier; it must be back at the garrison before the tide, or "I hang somebody for it" [00:10:05].
- The grey-cloaked woman: an unknown watcher on the tollhouse roof, then gone [00:15:30]. Only Rook saw her [00:16:40].

Forgotten threads
- Nothing yet; every thread is one session old. The grey woman is the closest: Rook asked about her and nobody followed up [00:16:10].

NPCs in play
- Hedda Brask, toll keeper: broad, slow-spoken, never looks up from the ledger [00:01:40]. Wants the ferry bell back [00:12:50]. Married to Osric; they run the crossing together (game master).
- Osric Brask, ferryman: lean, talks fast, laughs at his own jokes [00:06:20]. Wants unknown. According to Osric, the bell was his father's [00:13:20]. "Hedda takes the toll, I take the oars. Brask and Brask." [00:06:45]
- Warden Calloway: curt, mud to the knees, never dismounts, rides off without waiting for an answer [00:09:10, 00:10:40]. Wants her pay chest back before the tide [00:10:05]. No tie to the Brasks shown.

Clocks and pressure
- Spring tide: 0/4, shown to players; four days, then the causeway is gone until midsummer [00:09:40] (confirmed by the game master). There is no frame timeframe to measure it against.
- Without a clock: the chapel floods at high water, according to Osric [00:13:20]; the causeway is already half under water [00:00:15].

Off-screen moves
1. Calloway sends someone to keep watch. At dawn a garrison trooper waits at the tollhouse, wants to know what the party has learned for the warden, and watches who crosses. Built on: Calloway's pay chest [00:10:05]; she rode toward the garrison [00:10:40].
2. Someone got to the chapel first. At the fifth bell the party finds fresh, wet footprints leading through their marked door. Built on: the grey-cloaked woman on the roof [00:15:30]; the marked door [00:18:45]; low tide at the fifth bell [00:20:10].
3. The drowning causeway calls Osric away. At dawn a stranded carter shouts for the ferry, and Osric must row just as the party sets out. Built on: the causeway half under water [00:00:15]; "When the causeway drowns, I row folk across" [00:06:45].

Frame flags
- The frame is empty: no goal, timeframe, stakes or finale yet.

What next
1. A short frame talk for Brackwater: goal, timeframe and stakes (recommended).
2. Pick an off-screen move, then go to the first prep section.
3. Go straight to the first prep section.

Your answers are in the draft. Character concepts, a Calloway–Brask tie and the courier's identity stay blank, as the table left them. This is the revised briefing:

**Where the party stands**
Night at the Brackwater tollhouse, by Osric's fire [00:19:30]. The party found the drowned chapel flooding, marked its door and turned back [00:18:45]. Brother Fen guarded the cart throughout and heard everything, but said nothing (game master). Player plan: return at low water tomorrow morning [00:14:05].

**What pulls**
- **Osric's ferry bell:** Hedda's condition stands: the bell first, then the ledger (game master). According to Hedda: "You bring that bell back to me and I open the ledger for you. Not before." [00:12:50]. According to Osric, low tide at the fifth bell gives "an hour in that chapel, no more" [00:20:10].
- **Find the red-cloaked courier:** the party's aim [00:02:20]. Who crossed with them is in Hedda's ledger, which "stays shut for strangers" [00:04:10].
- **Calloway's pay chest:** according to Calloway it crossed with the courier. It must be back at the garrison before the tide, or "I hang somebody for it" [00:10:05].
- **The grey-cloaked woman:** an unknown watcher on the tollhouse roof, then gone [00:15:30]. Only Rook saw her [00:16:40].

**Forgotten threads**
- Nothing yet, because every thread is one session old. The grey woman comes closest: Rook asked about her and nobody followed up [00:16:10].

**NPCs in play**
- **Hedda Brask, toll keeper:** broad and slow-spoken, never looks up from the ledger [00:01:40]. Wants the ferry bell back [00:12:50]. Married to Osric; they run the crossing together (game master).
- **Osric Brask, ferryman:** lean, talks fast, laughs at his own jokes [00:06:20]. Wants unknown. According to Osric, the bell was his father's [00:13:20]. "Hedda takes the toll, I take the oars. Brask and Brask." [00:06:45]
- **Warden Calloway:** curt, mud to the knees, never dismounts, rides off without waiting for an answer [00:09:10, 00:10:40]. Wants her pay chest back before the tide [00:10:05]. No tie to the Brasks shown.

**Clocks and pressure**
- **Spring tide:** 0/4, shown to players. In four days the causeway is gone until midsummer [00:09:40] (confirmed by the game master). There is no frame timeframe to measure it against.
- **No clock:**
  - According to Osric, the chapel floods at high water [00:13:20].
  - The causeway is already half under water [00:00:15].

**Off-screen moves**
1. **Calloway sends someone to keep watch.** At dawn a garrison trooper waits at the tollhouse, wants to know what the party has learned for the warden, and watches who crosses. *Built on:* Calloway's pay chest [00:10:05]; she rode toward the garrison [00:10:40].
2. **Someone got to the chapel first.** At the fifth bell the party finds fresh, wet footprints leading through their marked door. *Built on:* the grey-cloaked woman on the roof [00:15:30]; the marked door [00:18:45]; low tide at the fifth bell [00:20:10].
3. **The drowning causeway calls Osric away.** At dawn a stranded carter shouts for the ferry, and Osric has to row just as the party sets out. *Built on:* the causeway half under water [00:00:15]; "When the causeway drowns, I row folk across" [00:06:45].

**Frame flags**
- The frame is empty: no goal, timeframe, stakes or finale yet.

**What next**
1. A short frame talk for Brackwater: goal, timeframe and stakes (recommended).
2. Pick an off-screen move, then go to the first prep section.
3. Go straight to the first prep section.
